chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
"Pre-emption is according to the number of men."

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report agrees with the opinions of some of the Sunnis, but we do not adopt it. And that upon which we act is what we have previously stated, that preemption is established if the property is between two persons; but if they increase (in number), there is no preemption for one of them.

key_terms.الشُّفْعَةُ: Pre-emption (right of first refusal in property sale)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on pre-emption (Shuf'ah) when there are multiple co-owners?
ai.summary: This narration from the chain of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq presents a specific legal opinion regarding 'shuf'ah' (pre-emption), suggesting the right applies proportionally to the number of male co-owners. Shaykh al-Tusi records the commentary of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Furaykat, who notes that while this view aligns with some Sunni schools, the established Shia position limits the right to cases involving only two parties, excluding larger groups to prevent complexity. This highlights the Shia juristic preference for simplicity and clarity in property rights transactions.
